name: Ekacakrā
aka: Ekachakra, Ekacakra, Ekacakrā-dhāma, Garbhavāsa, Vīracandrapura, Birchandrapur
location: 8 miles east of Mallārapura station (Eastern Railway, loop line); 5½ kroś from Rāmpurhāṭ
about:
Appearance place and childhood pastimes of Nityānanda Prabhu (Garbhavāsa). Here the Pāṇḍavas lived in hiding.
(1) A stone altar in a temple marks Nityānanda Prabhu's birth room; beside it a great banyan where his ṣaṣṭhī-pūjā was done. (2) Padmāvatī-puṣkariṇī, where his mother Padmāvatī bathed 21 days after his birth. (3) Mālātalā: an aśvattha at the door of the Garbhavāsa temple on whose branch Śrī Caitanya hung his garland. (4) Gaurāṅga and Nityānanda deities said to be installed by Rāghava Paṇḍita of Govardhana. (5) Siddha-bakula, a huge tree.
Vīracandrapura, named after Vīrabhadra Prabhu, lies within the eight miles of Ekacakrā: a large temple with Śrī Bāṅkā-rāya (Baṅkima-deva) installed by Vīrabhadra, with Jāhnavā Mātā on his right and Rādhikā on his left; also Muralīdhara, Rādhā-Mādhava and Manomohana. Festivals: Goṣṭhāṣṭamī, Rathayātrā and Nityānanda's appearance day.

name: Kheturī
location: Six kroś from Rāmpur Boāliyā. From Śiyāldaha by rail to Lālgolāghāṭ, by steamer across to Premtalī, then two miles to Kheturī
about:
Śrīpāṭa of Narottama Ṭhākura; the place of his birth (the old palace was north of the temple). The deities were damaged in the earthquake of 1897; the present temple is not from Ṭhākura Mahāśaya's time. West of it stood the large temple built by Rāja Santoṣa Datta of Gopālpur (its foundations remain), with Rādhākuṇḍa to the south and Śyāmakuṇḍa to the north. The stone (5 × 2 ft) on which Śrīnivāsa Ācārya and Narottama used to sit is still there, with a crack in the middle.
Narottama installed six deities here: Gaurāṅga, Vallabhīkānta, Vrajamohana, Kṛṣṇa… Other places at Kheturī: Āsanabāḍī, Āmalītalā (a 400-year-old tree said to have grown from his tooth-stick), Bhajana-ṭulī with a great banyan, and the Śyāmasāgara tank; samādhi of the devotee Rāmadāsa Bābājī.
Premtalī, one kroś south on the Padmā: Mahāprabhu came here and left prema in the Padmā for Narottama.

name: Pānihāṭi
location: Near Sodpur station, on the bank of the Gaṅgā
about:
Śrī Rāghava-bhavana: the house of Rāghava Paṇḍita. The banyan under which Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī held the daṇḍa-mahotsava (chipped-rice festival) still stands. Rāghava Paṇḍita's samādhi is in the house, under a bower of mālatī and mādhavī. «Rāghavera jhāli» and the service of his sister Damayantī are told in the main books.
Also the Gaurāṅga-bhavana of Amūlyadhana Rāya Bhaṭṭa.

name: Kumārahaṭṭa
location: One kroś west of Hālisahara station
about:
Appearance place of Īśvara Purī, at Kālikātalā in Mukhopādhyāya-pāḍā; his father was Śyāmasundara Ācārya. Nayana Bhāskara, Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura and Śrīrāma Paṇḍita lived here.
After Mahāprabhu took sannyāsa, Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita could not stay in Nadīyā without him and came here with his brothers: the site near the Caitanya-ḍobā (the new temple) and the Maṭha-puṣkariṇī is shown as Śrīvāsa's home.
According to this book, Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura was born at Nati (Nati-grāma, also called Khāsabāṭī), south of Hālisahara (most sources give Māmagāchi, in Navadvīpa); his mother Nārāyaṇī was the daughter of Śrīvāsa's elder brother Nalina Paṇḍita. The poet-sādhaka Rāmaprasāda Sena also lived at Hālisahara.

name: Kulīnagrāma
about:
Śrīpāṭa of (1) Haridāsa Ṭhākura, (2) Satyarāja Vasu (Satyarāja Khān), (3) Rāmānanda Vasu, (4) Śaṅkara, (5) Vidyānanda and (6) Vāṇīnātha Vasu.
The main temple is Śrī Madanagopāla's, with Rādhikā on the left and Lalitā on the right (installed long after; once he was alone), Nāḍu-gopāla and eight śālagrāmas — one, Śrīdhara, older than Satyarāja Khān. In front is the Gopāla-dīghi tank. A small Śiva-liṅga served by Satyarāja, Gopeśvara Śiva, with a bull whose inscription says it was installed by Satyarāja. Also the bhajana-sthāna of Haridāsa Ṭhākura, less than a quarter mile from the Madanagopāla temple.
Festival from Pauṣa pūrṇimā to Māgha pūrṇimā. Rāmānanda Vasu's large family still lives in Bengal and Cuttack.

name: Śrīkhaṇḍa
about:
Śrīpāṭa of the Ṭhākuras of Khaṇḍa: Narahari Sarakāra Ṭhākura, Mukunda Ṭhākura, Raghunandana, Cirañjīva, Sulocana, Dāmodara, Rāmacandra Kavirāja, Govinda Kavirāja, Balarāma dāsa, Ratikānta, Rāmagopāla dāsa, Jagadānanda and other old Vaiṣṇavas of Śrīkhaṇḍa.
The festival of Narahari Sarakāra Ṭhākura's disappearance (Agrahāyaṇa kṛṣṇa dvādaśī) is held in the Baḍaḍāṅgā field.

name: Kāṭwā
location: Kāṭwā station (Eastern Railway, Bāṇḍel–Bārhāroyā branch); one mile from the station to the Gaṅgā
about: Here Mahāprabhu took sannyāsa from Keśava Bhāratī. Temple of Mahāprabhu established by Gadādhara dāsa (Dāsa Gadādhara). To see: (1) the place where Mahāprabhu's head was shaved, west inside the temple grounds; (2) east of it, the samādhi of his hair; (3) the samādhi of Gadādhara dāsa; (4) inside a wall, the place of Keśava Bhāratī's sādhana and siddhi; (5) in front, the samādhi of Madhu the barber; (6) the samāja of Veṇīmādhava Ṭhākura, sevāyet of the temple; (7) the wonderful deity of Mahāprabhu installed by Gadādhara dāsa, and a later Nityānanda deity.

name: Ambikā-Kālnā
aka: Kalna, Kālnā, Ambika Kalna, Ambikā, Amvika Kalna, Āmuyā Muluka
location: Kālnā station, 51 miles from Hāoḍā (Eastern Railway); the śrīpāṭa is a mile and a half from the station
about:
Śrīpāṭa of Gaurīdāsa Paṇḍita, one of the twelve gopālas (Subala sakhā in Kṛṣṇa-līlā); his tirobhāva is on Śrāvaṇa śukla trayodaśī. Also the śrīpāṭa of his brother Sūryadāsa Paṇḍita, of Hṛdaya Caitanya (Śyāmānanda Prabhu's guru), of Paramānanda Gupta and of Kṛṣṇadāsa Sarakhela.
At the entrance an old tamarind (Āmalitalā): Mahāprabhu rested under it and there first met Gaurīdāsa; the trunk fell, but a new root came down from it and the tree grew again. A brass ratha of 1165 sāl, the nāṭa-mandira and the main temple. Also an old Gītā manuscript said to be in Mahāprabhu's own hand, and an oar (baiṭhā) of Mahāprabhu.
Gaurīdāsa installed here the two deities of Gaura-Nityānanda in their presence.

name: Śāntipura
location: By rail from Rāṇāghāṭ junction (Eastern Railway). Lat. 23°15', long. 88°29'
about: Śrīpāṭa of Advaita Ācārya. In his house: the Nṛsiṁha śilā and Śrī Madanagopāla. The line of Advaita's grandson Mathureśa Gosvāmī (son of Balarāma) serves here (the «Choṭa Gosāi» or Sītānātha house).

name: Rāmakeli
location: Near old Gauḍa; from Māldaha station, about 22 kroś from the town, passing west of the Piyāsabāḍī dāk-bungalow
about:
Near the capital of Gauḍa. In the time of Sultan Bārbak Shāh (1468–74) Mukunda-deva, the grandfather of Rūpa and Sanātana, was a high officer of the government. When his son Kumāra-deva died at Bāklā-Candradvīpa, he brought his grandsons Rūpa, Sanātana and the others to his home at Rāmakeli. Jīva Gosvāmī, son of Vallabha (Anupama), was born here. Narasiṁha Ojhā, an ancestor of Advaita Prabhu, also lived here.
North of Rāmakeli is the Sanātana-dīghi; on its west bank stood Sanātana's house (now called Baḍabāḍī). North of Hussain Shāh's Golden Mosque the brick steps of Rūpa's Rūpasāgara remain; east of it was Rūpa's house, and west of it Vallabha's.
Mahāprabhu came to Rāmakeli and here met Rūpa and Sanātana.

name: Gopīvallabhapura
location: At the edge of Medinīpura district: from Sarḍihā station (S. E. Railway) eight kroś by motor bus, then four kroś on foot or by bullock cart, and across the Subarṇarekhā river
about: Śrīpāṭa of Rasikānanda Prabhu. The deity he received from the Rāja of Mayūrabhañja was named Gopīvallabha by Śyāmānanda Prabhu; Rasikānanda's descendants serve here.

name: Viṣṇupura
about:
Place of the pastimes of Śrīnivāsa Ācārya and his first resting place: he rested under an old aśvattha near the house of the late Rādhikānātha Gosvāmī, where there is a ruined temple. The capital became the main centre of Vaiṣṇava preaching; Rāja Gopāla Siṁha (1712) made every subject chant a fixed number of names daily.
Śrīpāṭa of (1) Rāja Vīra Hāmvīra, (2) Rāmadāsa, disciple of Śrīnivāsa, (3) Prasāda dāsa Kavipati, (4) Gokula dāsa Mahānta, (5) Vallavī Kavipati and (6) Vyāsācārya.
Famous temples: Śyāmarāya's pañca-ratna (1646), Joḍa-bāṅglā (1655), Kālācāṅda, Lālajī (1658), Muralīmohana (1652), Madanagopāla, Madanamohana (1694, built in Rāja Durjaya Siṁha's time); the Rādhā-Śyāma temple (1680 Śaka) near the Mṛnmayī Devī temple by the palace, with two pairs of Nitāi-Gaura; and the Dalamādala cannon.
